newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat bids seen worth $143-149 per tonne.
newsitem.headline: French wheat bids seen worth $143-149 per tonne.

text.p: Grain firms pitched for European wheat through France at between some $143 and $149 per tonne on Thursday, exporters said.
The lowest subsidy bid of 17.93 Ecus per tonne at a weekly European Union auction was very close to the maximum refund awarded last week when French wheat was worth more than $150.
The dollar has risen sharply since then, while domestic wheat prices have been relatively stable.
Traders said the lowest bid for an EU refund, with the greatest chance of success, equated to $149 a tonne for January.
That is about in line with U.S. soft red winter wheat.
Highest bids of 21.87 Ecus per tonne seemed closer to U.S. soft white wheat prices of around $143 per tonne, traders said.

The EU has been gradually decoupling its wheat exports from soft red winter prices -- seen as disproportionately firm in a weakening global market -- but says it is still in line with a pledge to the United States not to undercut its farmers.
Competition for sales gained a notch as the bids went in, with Egypt entering the market for 50,000 tonnes of French, U.S., Australian or Argentine wheat for January or February.
French domestic wheat at Rouen was trending about five francs a tonne higher after the bids, with buyers at 845 francs for January deliveries at Rouen and sellers asking 850 francs.
Prices exclude carrying charges which for January are 39.99 to 43.63 francs a tonne.
A wide range of bids for durum wheat reflects disagreement over the viability of EU durum on world markets after Brussels opened a trial tender to export 100,000 tonnes, traders said.
Exporters bid for 49,800 tonnes of EU durum at rebates between 4.98 Ecus and a high level of 30.00 Ecus per tonne.
Some traders have criticised last month's EU decision to open a tender, saying already firm domestic prices could be pushed up further by exports.
The lowest subsidy bids for barley of 30.50 Ecus per tonne broadly tracked recent EU prices around $133, traders said.
Traders bid between 30.50 Ecus and 32.00 Ecus.
The EU is under pressure to raise refunds to allow European traders a chance of fulfilling a Saudi purchase of 500,000 tonnes of barley at $154-156 per tonne.
The freight from Europe is said to be worth $25 per tonne.
